To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the European experience shows that policies designed to improve the health situation of Roma people need to: 1) be based on sound evidence and evaluation; 2) be comprehensive; 3) be based on a strong political commitment; 4) be based on inter-sectoral policy co-ordination; and 5) involve Roma communities in their design and implementation.
Roma people face a wide range of barriers to health and well-being.
the European Union and its Member States have developed a range of policy initiatives to tackle the social exclusion of Roma people.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the health of Roma in Europe and the policies that affect it.
the following questions: What is being done to tackle the social exclusion and poor health outcomes of Roma people?
the following issues: the health of the Roma population in Europe, the health inequalities that they experience, and the policies that have been developed to address these issues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no conclusive statement on what works to improve the health of Roma communities.
the European Region is still far away from the goal to improve the situation of Roma communities.
there is a lack of conclusive statements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Roma population has a very high burden of health problems, and this is a major obstacle to their social inclusion and integration into the society.
the European Roma are the largest ethnic minority group, with an estimated population of 12–14 million people, living in 11 countries of Central and South Eastern and Eastern Europe.
the Roma population is a heterogeneous group with different health and social conditions and needs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Roma issue is a European issue.
Roma inclusion requires a comprehensive and integrated policy approach that goes beyond health.
there is a need for a paradigm shift in the approach to Roma policies.
